findings.title: verify-act.js and verify-state.js read A.package at top level without guarding it, unlike sibling verify-architecture.js
locations: instruments/check-consistency/workflow/verify-act.js:55 — `const PREAMBLE = `You are an ADVERSARIAL FIX AUDITOR for ${A.package.name} — ${A.package.description}`
instruments/check-consistency/workflow/verify-state.js:49 — `const PREAMBLE = `You are an ADVERSARIAL CLOSURE AUDITOR for ${A.package.name} — ${A.package.description}`
findings.description: Both verify-act.js and verify-state.js build their PREAMBLE as a plain top-level const (evaluated immediately, not deferred in a function) that dereferences A.package.name/.description unconditionally. Neither script's required-args guard list includes 'package'. If the CLI ever omits it, the script throws an uncaught TypeError the instant it loads, crashing the entire verification stage for every unit at once, rather than failing one lane with a named error. Sibling verify-architecture.js uses A.package.name identically (line 33) and correctly guards it (line 17), showing this is an omission.
findings.resolution_hint: Add 'package' to the required-arg list in both verify-act.js and verify-state.js, matching verify-architecture.js.

findings.title: Every one of the 11 workflow scripts writes A.schema_version into its banked artifact without validating it was supplied
findings.description: Every companion instruments/*/schema.json lists schema_version as a required top-level args property, and every one of the 11 scripts embeds A.schema_version into the artifact it directs an agent to Write — either as a JS field later passed to JSON.stringify, or interpolated directly into a Write-instruction string. None of the 11 scripts' own required-arg guard lists includes schema_version. JSON.stringify({schema_version: undefined, ...}) silently omits the key entirely, and a template literal with ${undefined} renders the literal text 'undefined'. Either way a missing schema_version produces a banked artifact silently lacking a field every lane_file/schema.json declares required, exactly the failure mode the guard pattern exists to prevent — except for this one universal field.
findings.resolution_hint: Add 'schema_version' to the required-arg guard list in all 11 scripts.

findings.title: rubric-audit.js's Blind-run pipeline stage converts a dead agent into a truthy 'reported nothing' result, so a dead hat is never flagged dead
findings.description: Stage 1 of the pipeline() call always resolves to a truthy object, even when agent() died and returned null — the .then() wraps it unconditionally. Stage 2's liveness check (if (!run) return null) can therefore never fire from a stage-1 death, and the final dead computation on line 127 can likewise never see it. A blind-run hat that crashes is indistinguishable from one that genuinely found nothing: every finding id assigned to it is scored MISSED, silently corrupting the rubric audit's tally with no DEAD signal anywhere — the opposite of the pattern lanes.js, panel.js, audit.js and hunt.js all follow.
findings.resolution_hint: In stage 1, return null (not a wrapped object) when the agent died, e.g. `.then(r => r ? { key, ids, reported: r.findings || [] } : null)`, and track dead keys explicitly before scoring.

findings.title: verify-act.js's mode=batches guard claims full coverage but only checks that the batches array is non-empty
locations: instruments/check-consistency/workflow/verify-act.js:143 — under-graded check compares against u.items.length, not total coverage
findings.description: `if (!batches.length) throw new Error('mode=batches needs a non-empty batches array covering EVERY finding')` (line 103) states in its own error text that batches must cover every finding, but the code never checks that the ranges in A.batches actually partition 1..A.findings.length with no gap or overlap. A gap between batch ranges silently produces zero items for those findings, and nothing downstream (the got < u.items.length check on line 143, or the written/dead/empty/truncated bookkeeping) can detect a finding that fell into such a gap: it is never assigned to any unit, never graded, and never reported as dead, empty, or truncated.
findings.resolution_hint: After building units in batches mode, assert the union of batch ranges equals 1..A.findings.length (e.g. sum of unit item counts equals A.findings.length) and throw if not.

findings.title: Four sibling scripts each require a schema arg they never read in the script body
locations: instruments/audit-changes/workflow/audit.js:2,21 — `kind` ('the kind switch' per the header comment) is required and validated but never branched on anywhere in the file
instruments/bug-hunt/workflow/hunt.js:11,20 — `witness_env` is required by instruments/bug-hunt/schema.json but never referenced in hunt.js
instruments/check-consistency/workflow/panel.js:22-23 — `cost` and `opened` are both required by instruments/check-consistency/schema.json but neither appears anywhere in panel.js

instruments/check-docs/workflow/lanes.js:19 — `package` is required by instruments/check-docs/schema.json but A.package never appears in lanes.js's body, unlike sibling panel.js/audit.js/hunt.js which each build an explicit package-identity preamble from it
findings.description: Across the four instruments, several args each script's own guard-list forces the CLI to supply are never consumed once validated — most notably 'kind' in audit.js, which the file's own provenance comment credits to an inherited 'kind switch' that does not exist in this rewrite, and 'package' in lanes.js, which alone among the four lane-fan-out scripts never surfaces the package's name/description/deliberate absences to its own prompt text.
findings.resolution_hint: Either wire each unused arg into the prompt/behaviour its schema and comments describe, or drop it from the schema's required list and the script's guard if genuinely no longer needed.

findings.title: verify-act.js threads the CLI-computed 'expected' verdict count into each unit but never uses it as a completeness check
locations: src/CLI/Passes.jl:358,433 — expected_act is computed independently from the banked findings before this script runs
findings.description: A.lanes[].expected (documented in schema/pass.schema.json as 'lane → expected verdict count', computed independently at Passes.jl:358/433) is stored on each unit, but the under-graded check on line 143 compares the returned verdict count only against u.items.length — a count derived from filtering the same A.findings array this script was handed. Because both sides come from the same input, the check can never catch a finding dropped, duplicated, or mis-tagged with the wrong lane before it reached this script.
findings.resolution_hint: Compare got (and u.items.length) against u.expected as well, and flag a lane whose expected/actual/items-length trio disagree.

findings.title: hunt.js's free-lane preamble never explains candidates_found, unlike the territory-lane preamble
locations: instruments/bug-hunt/workflow/hunt.js:68-74 — FREE_PREAMBLE (no mention of candidates_found or a cap)
instruments/bug-hunt/workflow/hunt.js:76-84 — HUNT_PREAMBLE explains candidates_found against a stated cap of 6
instruments/bug-hunt/workflow/hunt.js:25-47 — CANDIDATE_SCHEMA requires candidates_found identically for every lane
findings.description: CANDIDATE_SCHEMA requires candidates_found from every lane, and for territory lanes HUNT_PREAMBLE explains exactly what it means and why (the truncation signal against a stated cap of 6). FREE_PREAMBLE, used for the free/unconstrained lane, states no cap and never mentions candidates_found at all, so that lane has no textual basis for reporting it meaningfully — most likely it will just echo candidates.length, degrading the truncation signal for the one lane whose brief is to catch what a capped lane could not.
findings.resolution_hint: Add one sentence to FREE_PREAMBLE telling the free lane what candidates_found means for it.
